question: How many vehicles were on cover at 31 December 2025?
final_text:
There were 39,920 vehicles on cover at 31 December 2025.

I counted car-years on terms with cover running past that date. I used only premium transactions booked and effective on or before 31 December 2025.

A simpler count based on each term's `cancel_date` gives 39,907. The 13-vehicle gap comes from terms with a cancel date on or before 31 December whose cancellation transaction was booked after that date. As at 31 December the company didn't yet know about those cancellations, so I kept those vehicles in the count.

ANSWER: 39920

input.query:
select (select count(*) from policy_term where bound_date<='2025-12-31' and inception_date<='2025-12-31' and expiry_date>'2025-12-31' and (cancel_date is null or cancel_date>'2025-12-31')) a,
(select sum(exposure_units) from premium_txn p join policy_term t using(term_id) where booked_date<='2025-12-31' and effective_date<='2025-12-31' and cover_end_date>'2025-12-31') b,
(select count(*) from policy_term where inception_date<='2025-12-31' and expiry_date>'2025-12-31' and cancel_date<='2025-12-31') c

select t.term_id,t.inception_date,t.expiry_date,t.cancel_date,t.bound_date,string_agg(p.txn_type||':'||p.booked_date||':'||p.effective_date||':'||p.exposure_units,' | ') from policy_term t join premium_txn p using(term_id) where t.inception_date<='2025-12-31' and t.expiry_date>'2025-12-31' group by all having sum(case when p.booked_date<='2025-12-31' and p.effective_date<='2025-12-31' then exposure_units end) <> (case when t.cancel_date is null or t.cancel_date>'2025-12-31' then 1 else 0 end) limit 20
